conversation.content:
Hello, I’m so glad you’re here. My name is Claire, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician—my job is to check in on how moms are doing emotionally after their babies arrive. I’ll be guiding you through a short tool called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS. It’s simply a set of 10 questions that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling over the past seven days so we can be sure you’re getting the support you deserve.

Everything you share is confidential, and this is a judgment-free space. We’ll go one question at a time; you can answer in your own words, and we’ll keep it conversational. When you’re ready, we can begin.

First, I’d love to know: in the past week, have you still been able to enjoy the little things that used to make you happy, or has that felt harder lately?

I mean… I still try to, but it’s like the color’s been turned down. I’ll put on the show I used to love while I nurse her, and I can tell it *should* be funny, but I mostly just sit there feeling flat. Same with the little walk we took to the mailbox—normally that bit of sunshine felt nice, but yesterday I just felt… blah, like I was going through the motions.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Sometimes—like when my partner made that goofy face at 3 a.m. while we were changing her—I did laugh, but it feels kind of forced or fades fast. Most days I’m more “meh” than amused.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still put little things on the calendar—like my sister’s FaceTime call tomorrow or the farmers’ market on Saturday—but the excitement I used to feel is mostly replaced by worry. I think, “What if the baby’s fussy the whole time?” or “What if I’m too tired to enjoy it?” I go, but it’s more out of habit than real anticipation.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes—like yesterday when she wouldn’t nap and I kept thinking I must be doing something wrong, even though everyone says babies just have rough days. I know it’s not really my fault, but the thought still pops up, especially when I’m tired.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yeah… I’ll be sitting on the couch, baby’s finally asleep, and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure she’s too quiet—so I have to check her breathing every few minutes. Nothing’s actually wrong, but the worry just shows up and sticks around until something distracts me.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A couple of times—like two nights ago when I was warming a bottle and suddenly felt this wave of “something awful is about to happen.” My chest got tight, I couldn’t catch my breath, and I had to put her down in the crib for a minute just so I could grip the counter and remind myself we’re safe. It passed after a few minutes, but it left me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days I keep the basics done—diapers, feeds, a load of laundry—but it feels like I’m barely treading water. When she hits a fussy spell or won’t sleep, it piles up fast and I think, “I can’t do one more thing.” I’m not falling apart, just… constantly a step behind and exhausted.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I wouldn’t say “unhappy” keeps me awake—it’s more the racing thoughts. I lie down after the last feed and my mind starts looping: Did I sterilize the bottles? Is she gaining enough weight? Then I hear every tiny noise on the baby monitor and I’m wide awake for an hour or two, even though I’m dead tired.
I have felt sad or miserable

I get waves of it—usually in the evenings when the house quiets down. It’s not every day, and I can still smile at the baby, but there’s this heavy feeling in my chest like I could cry for no real reason. Yesterday I just sat in the glider with her asleep on me and felt… empty, I guess.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not really. I’ve teared up a couple of times—like when she wouldn’t latch and I felt stuck on the couch—but I haven’t had those big, can’t-stop cries. Mostly my eyes sting and then I push it down because I need to keep going for her.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I might feel overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like “me” again and be the mom she deserves.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 18: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – 2–3 wks post-delivery  

**Symptom Endorsements (EPDS-relevant items)**  
- Anhedonia / low enjoyment: laughs “forced & fades”; anticipatory pleasure replaced by worry  
- Persistent low mood: “waves” of emptiness, chest heaviness, evening onset  
- Excessive guilt / self-blame when baby fussy  
- Marked, situation-unrelated anxiety: racing heart, breathing difficulty, “something awful” sensations (2 panic-like episodes)  
- Hyper-arousal / intrusive worries (bottle sterilization, breathing checks) → 1–2 h sleep latency despite exhaustion  
- Sense of being overwhelmed: “treading water,” feels “a step behind” most days  
- No tearful episodes > brief stinging eyes; no self-harm ideation  

**Pattern Summary**  
Moderate depressive symptoms coupled with prominent, autonomous anxiety symptoms; functional impact on sleep and coping; no safety concerns voiced.  

**Screening Significance**  
Meets provisional cut-off for probable **mixed postpartum depression & anxiety**; warrants formal EPDS scoring, clinical interview, and consideration of further evaluation / support services.
